A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ASB study. All 36 pages in each version, including Appendices A–F, are readable, and their text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V3 reports original ASB experiments across 13 LLM backbones, including attack, defense, and utility results in Section 5 and Appendix D.

after.justification: V4 retains these original experiments, including attack-combination comparisons, backdoor-trigger evaluations, and defense results.

M1.justification: The agent framework, PoT backdoor procedure, prompt-injection and memory-poisoning methods, and defenses remain unchanged in Section 4 and Appendix A.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ASB scenarios, agents, tasks, and tools, including aggressive and non-aggressive instructions. No evaluated domain or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The attack and defense comparator sets remain identical in the corresponding experiments, including the four attack combinations in Table 14 and defenses in Tables 7–8 and 19–21.

E3.justification: The simulated-tool evaluation, 13 LLM backbones, seven metrics, and PoT demonstration/test-task selection remain unchanged. Section 5.2 and Appendix C introduce no revised experimental settings.

E4.justification: Appendix D retains the same attack-combination, trigger, utility, instruction-type, task-aggressiveness, and detection-threshold analyses. Removing explanatory prose about IPI+MP does not remove its experiment or supporting table.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same point-estimate reporting. Neither reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Numerical results are unchanged, but qualitative reporting changes: Section 5.3 describes the rise-then-fall ASR relationship using agents’ utility instead of LLM capability. Appendix D.1.2 also removes the prose finding of reduced IPI+MP effectiveness, although Table 14 retains its 23.75% average ASR and −3.80 percentage-point delta.

T1.justification: The formal attack definitions, threat-model assumptions, mathematical objectives, and metric definitions remain unchanged, including Equations 1–20.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction’s contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about ASB’s coverage, the novel PoT attack, agent vulnerabilities, limited defense effectiveness, and the NRP metric.

C2.justification: Appendix D.1.2 removes the proposed explanation that contextual manipulation by IPI and long-term memory poisoning can conflict, reducing attack effectiveness. V4 supplies no replacement mechanism; the other substantive interpretations and qualifications remain.

D1.justification: Benchmark-generation details, prompts, model configurations, memory storage, output parsing, simulated-tool implementation, and code-access instructions remain unchanged in Appendices B, C, and F.

R1.justification: The cited works, Section 2 positioning, and Appendix B.3 comparison with InjecAgent and AgentDojo are unchanged. No prior work or novelty relationship is added or removed.

P1.justification: V4 makes localized capitalization, grammar, tense, and terminology edits in Sections 5.2–5.3 and Appendix D, alongside the short D.1.2 deletion. The section order and overall narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 15 moves from page 31 to page 30, and subsequent appendix text, tables, and Figure 4 shift through reflow. The ethics statement now fits on page 35. No figure or table is added, removed, or substantively redesigned.

improvement.justification: The methods, numerical evidence, and reproducibility information remain intact. V4 lightly polishes wording and removes a speculative IPI+MP explanation, but also drops prose highlighting its negative result; unchanged Table 14 preserves that evidence. These localized edits leave the paper’s overall scientific support and usability essentially unchanged.
